entities.summary: Eanmund of Kent was a 9th-century King of Kent, jointly with Sigered of Kent, from around 825 to 830. He was the ruler of Kent during the Viking invasions of England and played a crucial role in the region's defense. Eanmund's reign was marked by several battles against the Vikings, including the Battle of the Thames, where he inflicted significant casualties on the enemy. Despite his efforts, Kent was eventually conquered by the Vikings in 835. Eanmund's legacy lies in his resistance against the Viking invasions, which has been remembered in historical accounts as a testament to the bravery and resilience of the Kentish people. The Eanmund of Kent's reign also saw the construction of several fortified settlements, including the town of Rochester, which became a key stronghold against the Vikings. Eanmund's story serves as a reminder of the complex and often tumultuous history of medieval England.
